summary: Nyingcha Duoji specializes in Tibetology. He studied at Boston University and Harvard University, where he earned his PhD under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, committee member Janet Gyatso, and teacher Mark C. Elliott.

Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (1932–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Katok Monastery under Penor Rinpoche, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, later teaching numerous prominent students.
Nyoten Jimbo (1880–1946) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Baisen Azegami and held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner by 2009 and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Paris (~1946–1948), Harvard University (~1948–1950), and Princeton University (~1950–1955), later holding posts at the University of Michigan (~1954–1969) and Harvard University (~1969–1990).

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (attested 1892).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Ceylon and SOAS under William Stede and Betty Heimann, he headed Sanskrit at Ceylon and held visiting roles at Pennsylvania, Harvard, and Smith College.
Oliver Philipp Frey works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and later held an academic post there.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1925–1928) and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1934–1939), later holding posts at Paris (~1947–1970) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Harvard, Washington, and Copenhagen under scholars including Tord Olsson and Karl H. Potter, and served as ansvarig utgivare at Lund University (attested 2000–2005).

Om Prakash is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma and Bisheshwar Prasad, later serving at Kirori Mal College and as professor of economic history at Delhi.

Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute, with Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and University of Hamburg.

Osamu Hayashima (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Having studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and researched at the University of Hamburg, he held professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Takata (1907–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied under Baiei Henmi and served as the head of the art department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.
Oscar Botto (1922–2008) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Turin from around 1941 to 1945. He also founded the journal Indologica Taurinensia.

Oskar von Hinüber (born 1939) is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied under Paul Thieme and at Mainz, held a professorship at Mainz (~1973–1981), and served as professor at the University of Freiburg (~1981–2006).

Osmund Bopearachchi (born 1949) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Paul Bernard (~1983–1987) and took up a post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique around 1989.

Osvald Sirén (1879–1966) worked in sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1897–1900) and held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923) and the Nationalmuseum (1928–1945).

Othmar Frank (1770–1840) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and philosophy. After studying in Paris and London, he held professorships at the University of Bamberg (~1804–1807), University of Würzburg (~1821–1826), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1826).
Otoya Tanaka (1903–1989) was an Indologist. He studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo (~1924–1927) and later held an academic post at Chuo University (~1957–1974).
